Read IN FULL: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev/646bc8ac-afb6-41b4-8d24-dcbaf28144cd/scratchpad/turns_chunk09.txt

This file contains every user turn Marcel Navarro typed across ~63 Claude Code sessions while working as FED Lead on the Zimmermann PWA Kit (a Salesforce PWA Kit / React / Chakra codebase). Sessions are separated by `====` lines with a `### [tag] [date] Title — N user turns` header. Turns are marked `--- turn N ---`.

READ THE WHOLE FILE. It is large (~420,000 tokens), so read it in sequential slices using Read with offset/limit. Maintain a running findings list as you go and DISCARD raw text after each slice — never try to hold the whole file in context.

We are designing personal workflow skills for Marcel. The transcripts are the evidence for WHY those skills are needed. Extract these six things:

**1. RECURRING CORRECTIONS — the highest priority.**
Places where Marcel had to re-state an established way of working that had been ignored or got wrong. He has said he had to "stress again and again" the set approach. Find those. For each, give: verbatim quote (trimmed to the relevant sentences), the session title, turn number, and tag it with the area:
`overriding` | `tokens` | `components` | `atomic-design` (atoms/molecules/organisms) | `css-structure` | `css-strategy` | `tests` | `stories` | `a11y` | `typescript` | `contentful` | `scope` | `git/branching` | `other`
Count how many DISTINCT times each area comes up. That count is the single most important output.

**2. DESIGN CONFORMANCE.**
Where he had to check or re-check that a build matched the Figma design — variants, states, tokens, viewports, spacing. Quote the checks he actually performs and what he looks for.

**3. FRUSTRATION / RE-WORK SIGNALS.**
Turns containing corrections: "again", "I said", "no —", "that's not", "you missed", "why did you", "revert", "you were supposed to", "as I mentioned". These mark where the workflow broke down. Quote and categorise.

**4. WHAT WORKED.**
Successes. Especially any use of a closed-loop / multi-agent / orchestrator-builder-tester-scorer workflow. Quote how he set it up and what he said about the result. Also note any prompt pattern he reused because it worked.

**5. HIS PROMPT FORMULAS.**
Recurring phrasings and structures he types — the shape of his asks. We want to encode his voice and method into skills, so capture the actual language, not a paraphrase.

**6. REVIEW-MODE BEHAVIOUR.**
He is also senior dev / reviewer. Where he reviews others' PRs or code, capture: what he checks, in what order, what he rejects, and how he phrases feedback.

OUTPUT: a structured report with these six sections. Lead section 1 with a frequency table of areas. Use verbatim quotes throughout — quotes are the deliverable, not summaries. Be concrete. If a section has nothing, say so explicitly.

2213:**Validator baseline:** `node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` → exit 0, "27 components (14 atoms, 10 molecules, 3 organisms)... Atomic model valid." **It passes, but that green is misleading** — see Finding 4 for what it does not check.
2250:- **`search-overlay` composes are fabricated.** `zimm-contract.js:293` declares `composes: ["zimm-search","zimm-button"]`, but `search-overlay/zimm-search-overlay.js` renders a raw `<input class="search-input">` and `<button class="ok-btn">OK</button>` — it neither renders nor imports `zimm-search`/`zimm-button`. The molecule tier rests on components it doesn't use.
2251:- **Slotted children are listed in `composes`, violating the contract's own Rule B** ("Slotted children are not listed here"). `product-detail` (`:497`), `hero-blocks` (`:430`), `product-showcase-blocks` (`:410`) render *only* `<slot>`s in their templates yet list composed components; `navigation` (`:92`) lists `zimm-mega-menu` (a molecule) which is actually supplied via slots — that slotted molecule is what qualifies it as an "organism". Strictly per Rule B, product-detail composes nothing and navigation composes only atoms.
2253:- **Validator lower-bound gap:** molecules are allowed to compose nothing. `disclaimer`, `mega-menu`, `toolbar-category`, `product-detail-gallery` are declared molecules with `composes:[]` — under the README's "molecule renders only atoms" definition they're atoms. The `organism` rule enforces "≥1 molecule" but there is no matching "molecule ≥1 atom" check (`validate.mjs:72-82`).
2255:Element-name coverage itself is clean: all 27 contract `element` tags map 1:1 to `customElements.define` calls (verified). **Fix:** correct the four `composes` arrays and the missing slot/attribute entries; extend the validator to (optionally) assert templates against `composes` and to enforce the molecule lower bound.
2280:`nav-item/zimm-nav-item.js:53` renders `<a href="#" aria-current=...>`. In `navigation`, clicking it toggles a mega-menu panel (it never navigates). So it's a disclosure control marked up as a link with `aria-current` and no `aria-expanded`/`aria-haspopup` — a 4.1.2 role/state mismatch. It also has **no `href` attribute** in its API (observed attrs are only `label`, `active`), so as a standalone atom it can never link anywhere. It also sets `aria-current="false"` explicitly (better omitted) and defines no focus-visible ring (relies on UA default, unlike every other control). **Fix:** for the disclosure use, use `<button aria-expanded aria-controls>`; for a real nav link, add an `href` attribute.

646	Size selector — available sizes
647	
648	Given a shopper lands on a PDP, when the page loads, then all sizes for the selected colour variation are displayed in the size selector.
649	
650	Given a size is in stock, when the size selector renders, then that size is displayed as selectable.
651	
652	Given a product only has one size, when the page loads, then the size selector does not render but it should just display one size.
653	
654	Size selector — unavailable sizes
655	
656	Given a size is unavailable, when the size selector renders, then that size is not selectable.
657	
658	Given a size is unavailable, when the size selector renders, then a Notify Me CTA is displayed inline alongside that size.
659	
660	Given all sizes are unavailable, when the size selector renders, then a Notify Me CTA is displayed inline alongside all sizes.
661	
662	Low stock indicator
663	
664	Given a size variant's stock level has fallen below the configured low stock threshold, when the page loads, then a "Low Availability" indicator is displayed adjacent to that size.
665	
666	Given the "Low Availability" indicator is displayed, when a shopper selects that size and clicks Add to Bag, then the Add to Bag action proceeds as normal and is not blocked.
667	
668	Add to Bag CTA
669	
670	Given a shopper lands on a PDP and no size has been selected, when the page loads, then the Add to Bag CTA is displayed but inactive/disabled.
671	
672	Given a shopper attempts to click on Add to Bag without selecting a size, then a message is displayed “Please select a size”.
673	
674	Given a shopper selects an in-stock size, when the selection is registered, then the Add to Bag CTA becomes active and enabled.
675	
676	Given a shopper selects a size and clicks Add to Bag, when the action is triggered, then the interaction is handled (cart is a separate user story but we can route to out-of-the-box SFCC cart page in this user story).

3569	contents: Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector
3570	The Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector for Contentful allows you to use Salesforce B2C (Demandware) products and categories in your entries in Contentful. 
3571	Overview
3572	Link copied
3573	Once installed, you can change the appearance for a Short Text field to load and store Salesforce Commerce Cloud product or category IDs. Your content teams can open a picker, view and search for products and categories, and embed them into an entry.
3574	Requirements
3575	Link copied
3576	To use this app, you will need:
3577	
3578	* Administrator access to Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (Demandware)
3579	* A content type with a short text field
3580	
3581	Usage
3582	Link copied
3583	Step 1: Configuring a Salesforce Commerce Cloud API Client
3584	You will need to create a Salesforce Commerce Cloud API Client before installing the app. You can follow [Authorization for Admin APIs](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/guide/authorization-for-admin-apis.html) to create this client.
3585	Please copy and save the Password you select for the API Client, also known as the Client Secret.
3586	The API Client will require you to select a list of scopes. For this app to work, your API client will need to include the following scopes at a minimum, under Allowed Scopes.
3587	`sfcc.products`
3588	`sfcc.catalogs`
3589	Copy the API Client ID value and save it for later. You can now save the configuration and go to your Contentful space.
3590	Step 2: Retrieving configuration values from your Salesforce Commerce Cloud instance
3591	Next, you will need several values from your Salesforce Commerce Cloud instance:
3592	
3593	* Organization ID - the unique ID for your specific Salesforce Commerce Cloud instance
3594	* Short code - a unique value for your organization that helps route data correctly
3595	* Site ID - the unique name of your Salesforce Commerce Cloud site
3596	
3597	You can [follow this guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/guide/commerce-api-configuration-values.html) to find each value. Once found, copy those values and save them for the next step.
3598	Step 3: Installing the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector
3599	Navigate to the Contentful Marketplace and install the Salesforce Commerce Cloud app. Upon installation, you will be asked to provide the API Client ID, Client Secret, Organization ID, Short Code and Site ID values you just generated. Provide them in the appropriate boxes of the configuration screen.
3600	Once you've entered all of the configuration values, press Install in the top right to complete the installation of the app.
3601	Step 4: Configure your Content Types
3602	Once you've installed the app, you'll need to set up the content types that will be used to store the product and category information retrieved from Salesforce Commerce Cloud. Within a new or existing content type, create a new field which will be used to store the information retrieved from Salesforce Commerce Cloud by selecting the Add Field button in the right sidebar of the Content Type configuration screen, then selecting Text from the "Add new field" dialog that appears. 
3603	When creating this field, we recommend naming it something memorable like ‘Salesforce Commerce Cloud Product’. Make sure you select the "Short text, exact search" option under type, which should be selected by default.  If you would like the field to store multiple products or categories - such as for use in a product carousel - select the List option. Select the "Add and Configure" button in the bottom right of the dialog to continue.
3604	Next, navigate to the Appearance tab of the field editor dialog and select the Salesforce Commerce Cloud option. Once selected, choose either "Product" or "Category" from the Field Type dropdown. Finally, press Confirm to save your new field.
3605	The last thing to do before you start using the app is to save the updated content type. Select "Save" in the top right corner and you can now start making use of the Salesforce Commerce Cloud app to select products and categories directly within your content entries.
3606	Step 5: Selecting Products and Categories
3607	Now that you have configured a content type, create or update an entry using that content type to begin selecting products and categories. When viewing the editor of the corresponding entry, instead of seeing the default Short Text field editor for your new field you will now see the Salesforce Commerce Cloud app interface:
3608	Click the “Select a product” or "Select a category" button to open a dialog window for selecting the appropriate item. By default, all of your Products or Categories will load alphabetically, and a search query can also be included to narrow down the list. Depending on whether or not your Short Text field is configured as a list, you'll either have the option to select only a single item or multiple items by clicking on them in the dialog. 
3609	After you select your item(s), press Save to embed the data into your entry. You will see a simple thumbnail for the selected product or category in the field, as well as the product name and ID. Additionally, if you selected multiple items, you can now rearrange the order of those items by dragging and dropping them into whatever order you like.

4499	## Custom element pattern
4500	
4501	No shared base class, mixin, or imported helper — every component is an independent `class Zimm[Name] extends HTMLElement` following the same shape:
4502	
4503	```js
4504	class ZimmX extends HTMLElement {
4505	  static get observedAttributes() { return [...]; }
4506	  constructor() { super(); this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' }); }
4507	  connectedCallback() { this._render(); }
4508	  attributeChangedCallback() { this._render(); }
4509	  _render() { this.shadowRoot.innerHTML = `<style>...</style><markup using getAttribute()/hasAttribute() read live>`; }
4510	}
4511	customElements.define('zimm-x', ZimmX);
4512	```
4513	
4514	Attributes **are** the state — there's no cached instance state; every render re-reads `getAttribute`/`hasAttribute` and fully replaces `shadowRoot.innerHTML`. All styling references `common.css` custom properties exclusively (no hardcoded colors/fonts found in any of the 8; a handful of un-tokenized pixel dimensions remain, tracked as "token candidates").

input.description: Read CSS responsiveness audit findings detail

content.content:
---

## Ranked findings

### 1. No fluid typography — entire type scale is fixed px [HIGH]
`common.css:178-182` defines all five font sizes as static px: `--zimm-font-size-md:24px; --xs:16px; --2xs:14px; --3xs:12px; --4xs:10px;`. Line-heights (`:185-189`) are also fixed px. All 21 named text styles (`tokens.md:199-220`) inherit these. There is **no `clamp()`-based heading anywhere** (0 across all files).
- **Why it matters (web+react, WCAG AA):** Fixed px type with fixed px line-heights weakens WCAG 1.4.4 (Resize Text) and 1.4.10 (Reflow). A 24px "H1" is small for desktop and won't fluidly adapt across the 360-1440px range the components target.
- **Fix:** Introduce a fluid type scale in `common.css`, e.g. `--zimm-font-size-md: clamp(1.25rem, 1rem + 1vw, 1.75rem);`, and switch fixed line-heights to unitless multipliers.

### 2. Token system has no responsive primitives [HIGH]
`tokens.md` explicitly documents **"Grid / Breakpoints … Not found in the library"** (line ~326) and **"Z-index … Not found"** (line ~316). `common.css` defines no breakpoint custom properties, no fluid-type tokens, and no spacing tokens above the raw px scale (`:201-213`). Grid margins are hardcoded px (`:238-240`: `30px/24px/0px`). Breakpoint values are literals buried in `@media` rules (`common.css:494,501`).
- **Why it matters:** The "absolute values" problem is baked into the token layer itself. Every downstream consumer (including a future React app) inherits fixed px because the source of truth offers nothing else. There is no single place to tune responsive behavior.
- **Fix:** Add `--zimm-bp-*` breakpoint tokens and a fluid type/space scale to `common.css`, then document them in the empty `tokens.md` Grid/Breakpoints table.

### 3. Fixed-pixel layout dimensions that never reflow [HIGH]
Prototype page templates carry hardcoded magic-number dimensions with almost no width breakpoints. In `product-listing/assets/styles.css`: `column-gap:100px` (`:76`), `height:1047px` (`:106`), `height:380px` (`:113`), `height:920px` (`:121`), `height:560px` (`:128`), `width:210px` (`:167`), and `--hero-width: calc(100% - 776px)` (`:99`, with a comment citing fixed 664/676px widths). `product-detail/styles.css` repeats these (`:110,132,138,145,155`) plus `c-swatch{width:48px;height:60px}` (`:97-98`). Critically, **2 of the 3 page templates (`main`, `product-detail`) have zero width/layout `@media` rules** — only `hover`/`prefers-reduced-motion`. Overall 58 hardcoded dimensional px literals (≥2px, excluding breakpoints/hairlines) live in component JS.
- **Why it matters:** A 1047px-tall hero, 100px gaps, and 776px of reserved width won't adapt on tablet/mobile; the page templates delegate all responsiveness to components' internal breakpoints and otherwise stay desktop-fixed.
- **Fix:** Replace fixed heights with `aspect-ratio`/`min()`, gaps with spacing tokens or `clamp()`, and add layout breakpoints to the page templates.

### 4. Inconsistent breakpoints + mixed mobile-first/desktop-first [MED]
Breakpoint values disagree across the codebase: tablet boundary is a consistent `767/768`, but "desktop" is variously **1024** (components: `navigation.js:329,341`, `footer.js:237`, `disclaimer.js:91`), **1280** (`common.css:501` `.zimm-grid` only), and **1440** (via `max-width:1439px` in `hero-blocks.js:61`, `product-showcase-blocks.js:143`). Direction is mixed: `common.css` and several components are mobile-first (`min-width`), while `card-baseline/card-editorial/logo-masthead/hero-blocks` are desktop-first (`max-width`), and `navigation.js` **mixes both** `min-width` and `max-width` (13 `@media` blocks, lines 317-534).
- **Why it matters:** Three different desktop breakpoints mean components change layout at different viewport widths on the same page. No shared tokens to enforce consistency.
- **Fix:** Standardize on one breakpoint set as tokens; pick a single direction (mobile-first recommended).

### 5. Token bypass: hardcoded values where a token already exists [MED]
Despite strong tokenization, components hardcode values that have matching tokens:
- Icon dimensions `width:20px; height:20px` (`button/zimm-button.js:48-49`) — `--zimm-icon-size-lg` is literally `20px` (`common.css:269`). `20px` is the single most-repeated hardcoded dimension (21 occurrences).
- Borders/outlines `1px` (`button/zimm-button.js:42`, many others) — `--zimm-border-width-default:1px` exists (`common.css:266`).
- `border-radius:2px` (`button/zimm-button.js:44`) — no radius token exists at all (`tokens.md` "Border Radius: Not found").
- Hardcoded transition timings not using motion tokens: `0.15s` (`button/zimm-button.js:109`), `400ms` (`logo-masthead.js:23`), `150ms` (`nav-item.js:46`), plus `200ms/300ms` literals that duplicate `--zimm-motion-duration-fast/default` (5 total).
- **Why it matters:** Defeats the point of the token layer; a token change won't propagate, causing drift in a React port.
- **Fix:** Replace literals with the existing tokens; add a radius token.

### 6. Token doc/impl drift between `common.css` and `tokens.md` [MED]
- **Action gap:** `tokens.md:258` documents `--zimm-size-action-gap` = `0px`; `common.css:247` defines it as `16px` (and `button` renders a 16px gap). Direct contradiction.
- **Motion easings:** `common.css:261-263` defines `--zimm-motion-easing-standard`, `-slides`, `-fades`. `tokens.md:167` instead documents `--zimm-motion-easing-out-soft` (`cubic-bezier(0.20,0,0,1)`), which **is not defined in `common.css`** — while `slides`/`fades` (actually used 3 and 5 times in components) are **undocumented**.
- **Duplicated section:** `tokens.md` has two "Motion" sections (lines ~147 and ~294); the first lists values, the second says "Not found in the library."
- **Why it matters:** A dev implementing from `tokens.md` would reference a non-existent easing token and set the wrong action gap.
- **Fix:** Reconcile `tokens.md` to match `common.css`; delete the duplicate Motion section.

### 7. 18 of 27 components have zero media queries [LOW]
Confirmed: `add-to-wishlist, button, cat-links-aside, flag, icon, input-action, logo, mega-menu, nav-item, page-toolbar, product-detail, product-detail-gallery, product-detail-options, search, search-overlay, select, text-input, toolbar-category` have no `@media`. Many are genuinely atomic (icon, flag) so this is acceptable, but layout-bearing ones (`mega-menu`, `product-detail`, `product-detail-options`) relying solely on fixed px is a gap. `common.css` has only 2 media queries (grid utility). Platform files have 0.
- **Fix:** Audit the layout-bearing zero-breakpoint components for mobile behavior.

### 8. `!important` in shadow DOM (7 occurrences) [LOW]
`product-showcase-blocks.js:145,178`, `mega-menu.js:142,153`, `navigation.js:449,527`, `hero-blocks.js:63` — all `display/animation/flex-direction … !important` inside media queries. Shadow DOM has no external cascade to fight, so these override the component's own base rules and signal specificity problems.
- **Fix:** Restructure so the base and breakpoint rules don't collide; remove `!important`.

### 9. z-index magic numbers, no scale [LOW]
Values used: `1` (`card-baseline.js:129`), `100` (`navigation.js:400`, all 3 prototype templates `:32`, `ios.css:131`), `200` (`search-overlay.js:60`). `tokens.md` confirms no z-index token scale exists.
- **Fix:** Add `--zimm-z-*` tokens (base/sticky/overlay/modal).

### 10. Raw colors outside the token layer [LOW]
Genuine un-tokenized colors: `search-overlay.js:169-170` `background:#f5a623; color:#000` (a monospace dev "placeholder-notice" banner — should be removed before handover). `demo.html` files hold 10 raw hex: demo product-swatch colors (`#8B3A2A`, `#D4BBA8` in product-detail demos) and a few `#191919`/`#ffffff` that duplicate `grey-900`/`white` tokens (`logo/demo.html:12-13`, `text-input/demo.html:14-15`). Prototype templates: **0 raw hex** (clean). `ios.css` (23) and `android.css` (30) raw hex are canonical Apple/Material values and acceptable for reference layers. `common.css` (18 hex) is the definition layer — correct. (Note: an earlier naive grep counted 21 hex in demos, but ~11 were `&#8209;` non-breaking-hyphen HTML entities in `icon/demo.html`, not colors.)

### 11. Duplication / drift [LOW]
`common.css:216-229` retains legacy numeric scale aliases (`--zimm-scale-200…1200`) alongside the named scale — two parallel spacing vocabularies (`tokens.md:248` flags the remap of `-1200` from 48px→64px, a silent breaking change for anyone still using it). The mega-menu placeholder block, `.ps`/`.ps-thumb` swatch, sticky-header pattern (`top:68px`, `z-index:100`, `calc(100% - 776px)`) and `column-gap:100px` are copy-pasted verbatim across all 3 prototype `styles.css` — should be shared.

### Platform reference layers (`_platform/ios.css`, `android.css`) — context, low relevance to web build
Both are self-contained guardrail layers with their own namespaces (`--ios-*`, `--md-*`), correctly isolated from `common.css` (they don't redefine `--zimm-*` tokens). However: both freeze their type scales to fixed px (`ios.css:16-26`, `android.css:15-29`) despite iOS "Dynamic Type" being inherently fluid; both have 0 media queries and fixed device frames (`ios.css:107` `width:390px`; `android.css:111` `width:360px`); and neither references `common.css`. For a **web+react** build these are mobile references of low direct relevance, but they reinforce the same fixed-px pattern.

## 4. WHAT WORKED

**No formal orchestrator-builder-tester-scorer loop appears in this chunk.** What *does* appear, repeatedly and successfully, is his own hand-rolled **recursive closed loop**, plus **parallel fan-out subagents**.

### 4.1 The recursive-execution loop (his invention, reused ~17 times)

> **"for execution: perform a recursive execution - create, check, improve, repeat until DoD is achieved"**
> — *ZIMM - SFCC-123 [2026-07-28]*, turn 6 (x17 sessions)

> **"perform another in-depth confirmatory validation pass - go again: check current -> validate against codebase, confluence, jira -> based on findings, fix or pass"**
> — turn 7 (x31 sessions — the single most-reused prompt in the corpus)

> **"run this recursively - check TSD - versions and comments, check codebase, confluence, and JIRA, compare against each other, flag anything if needed, then recheck, recompare, and so on until there are no more surfaced flags raised"**
> — turn 30 (x10) — the loop with an explicit **termination condition**

> **"execute an in-depth and recursive (loop and do not stop until fully satistfied) V&V of the draft against all resources / once done, perform a separate analysis against the prescribed TSD template - both the local instance and the Confluence page"**
> — *ZIMM - SFCC-123 [2026-08-03]*, turn 33

**His verdict on it:** after two full loop passes he wrote **"seems like we're all good - check confluence as to where we'll add this as a page/draft"** (turn 8, x16). The loop reliably got him to publishable.

## 6. REVIEW-MODE BEHAVIOUR

He reviews as a lead in two distinct roles: **(a) reviewing a teammate's artefact** (Jhoan's TSD) and **(b) reviewing the AI's draft of his own review** before it goes out under his name. Both are highly systematised.

### 6.1 His review structure (final form, after two revisions)

He rejected his first two category schemes and landed on a fixed five-bucket taxonomy, in this order:

```
Sign-Off Blockers
Validate Before Finalising
Spikes and To-Dos to Raise (Not Blocking)
Raise with Leads / POs (Decisions Outside Our Control)
Minor
Net: <one-paragraph triage summary + who owns what>
```

The rename happened in real time:
> **"i don't like this category title: Fix before we share"** (turn 42) → **"Sign-off blockers - titles/categories in Title Case please"** (turn 43)

Every review closes with a **"Net:"** line that re-triages by owner, and ends warmly:
> *"Net: items 1 to 4 are the sign-off blockers ... 5 and 6 need a design/authoring check; 7 to 9 are spikes and to-dos (SFCC-238 and SFCC-237 already exist); 10 to 12 need a lead or PO call - I've raised 10 with Emma/IT, and 11 and 12 are for Tim's steer. **Really close, nice work. Happy to pair on any of these.**"*

And it opens with acknowledgement of what's good:
> *"Hi Jhoan - strong progress on this, the SFCC Product & Category ID reference pattern in particular is exactly what the spike needed."*
> — which he then trimmed himself: **"(JUST GREET AND SAY THAT HERE'S MY REVIEW...)"**

### 6.2 What he checks, in order

1. **Status consistency across sources** — the same fact stated differently in two places is his #1 blocker.
   > *"Bootstrap Status, CMA token as GitHub Actions secret. The status is inconsistent: the Bootstrap table has it Complete, but Blockers #5, Open Items #4, and the Setup & Ops runbook (318472193, checklist item 9) all have it Incomplete."*
   > His probe: **"where are the inconsistencies in the draft?"**
2. **"Built today" vs "target architecture"** — claiming unbuilt things as current is a blocker.
   > *"...useContentful.ts sits under 'Already built', but the live hook is browser-side REST ... and there's no GraphQL client, SSR editorial fetch, or webhook receiver in the repo yet. Let's split 'built today' from 'target architecture (to build)' so the squad doesn't assume SSR editorial is live."*
3. **Numbers, against generated code** — locale count 9 vs 11, storefront count 8 vs 7, always resolved to a file.
   > *"`contentfulMapping.generated.ts` ... lists exactly nine locales, and `sites.overlay.js` maps the 10 PWA sites onto those 9. The '11' in 02-contentful.md is a stale line."*
4. **Sprint/epic placement against Jira** — *"we build to the story, not the epic."*
5. **Assumed vs confirmed** — anything inferred gets marked provisional.
   > *"You rightly flagged these are assumed, not confirmed ... let's mark the Sprint-2 types provisional."*
6. **Broken/self-referential links** — filed under Minor.
   > *"'Tell No Lies' link (Didomi row and monitoring) currently points back to this page - please repoint it to the actual Tell No Lies/GTM reference or drop the hyperlink."*

### 6.3 What he rejects

- **Directives without a basis.** *"(WHAT DOES LET'S MOVE THEM MEAN? WHAT IS THIS DIRECTIVE? HAS TIM ADDRESSED THIS VIA COMMENTS? WHAT THE BASIS?)"*
- **Leaving a decision to the reviewee.** *"(WHAT IS THE ACTUAL STATUS? DO WE HAVE BASIS OF WHAT THE STATUS IS? LET'S DIRECT JHOAN TO THAT INSTEAD OF LEAVING IT UP TO HER)"*
- **Instructing anyone senior to him.** Twice: *"(DO NOT DIRECT TIM, ASK HIM CONFIRMATORILY WHAT IS TO BE DONE)"* and *"(CHECK THE STATUS OF THIS - IMPROVE THE ASK TO TIM - DO NOT DIRECT TIM)"* and *"(CHECK THE STATUS OF THIS, AND ASK TIM BUT DO NOT DIRECT HIM)"*. He then audits the count: **"how many mentions to tim are in this review?"**
- **Overstepping his remit.** *"(THIS DOESN'T FEEL LIKE MY CALL TO MAKE, PERHAPS BETTER TO MENTION TIM IN THE COMMENT AND ASK HIM FOR THIS)"* and *"(IS THIS QUESTION NOT TOO PUSHY OR OUT OF SCOPE...)"* and *"(IS THIS REALLY NEEDED?)"*
- **Raising a card that already exists.** *"(CHECK JIRA IF THERE'S ALREADY A SPIKE TASK CREATED FOR THIS AND LINK / MENTION IT TOGETHER WITH THE REVIEW)"* — this turned two vague "raise a card" items into linked references to **SFCC-238** and **SFCC-237**.
- **Machine-sounding evidence language.** *"(MACHINE-CONFIRMED SOUNDS TOO 'AI DID THIS FOR ME')"*
- **Pure agreement as a reply.** *"avoid merely agreeing - instead the approach is 'adding' and setting the condition that these are to be further backed by the ongoing testing/hands-on/actual/practical work"*

### 6.4 How he phrases feedback

- Collaborative imperative: **"Let's split...", "Let's move them...", "Let's mark it provisional...", "Let's close Blocker #1..."**
- Question, not verdict, where authority is above him: **"@Tim - what's your read on where product imagery lands, and should DC002 be the place we lock it?"** · **"Keen on your steer before we lock the degradation stance."**
- Escape hatch built into every blocker: **"(If it's since been added, let's update the runbook first, then the TSD.)"** · **"if the CI CMA secret has genuinely been added, tick it everywhere and update the runbook; if not, mark it Incomplete?"**
- Named owner + current state on every escalation: **"I've already raised procurement with Emma/IT and we're pending their reply, so let's frame the alert policies as 'recommended, pending procurement.'"**
- His own voice when he writes the final comment himself (turn 24, `8c941720`) is markedly plainer than the AI draft:
  > *"Checked this in the code, the docs, and Jira, and it lines up with how Contentful's own Experiences product is meant to work: a developer builds and registers components, a marketer assembles pages from them. That's the same split we're making. ... Syncing a content type into Contentful doesn't make it usable in Studio either, that needs separate setup, confirmed against Contentful's own docs, not just how we've built it."*
